findings.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates (apple page)
findings.summary_md: As of 28 October 2026, Apple-shipped developer tools on macOS (git, curl, python3) still trust eight compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates whose private keys were exposed. The page notes Apple was notified on 17 October, and the 26 October macOS 27.2 update did not fix the issue and undid user-applied manual fixes.

findings.title: About the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs - Apple Support
findings.summary_md: Apple's support document (published 19 October 2026) states that since 19 October it has been blocking the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA TLS certificates in Safari, Mail, and apps using Apple's networking framework. It confirms the compromise spans multiple intermediates and that Apple is making additional updates.

findings.title: MacOS Certificate Crisis: Apple's Delayed Response to eMudhra Compromise - TechPlanet
findings.summary_md: TechPlanet reports on 28 October 2026 that over a week after Apple was notified (17 October), macOS command-line tools including git, curl, and python3 still trust the compromised certificates. The article frames the exposure as leaving developers vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks that could serve malicious clones or alter pushes.
